REWORK CARRY-THROUGH — every review disposition, one mechanism

A review is POST-stage: an approval, rejection or correction of that stage's output. It never sends the record back to be re-verified (the one exception: reextract). The disposition writes a pipeline_rework(record_type, record_id, stage, reason) row; partial unique index keeps one outstanding row per record+stage. The

housekeeping run — Argo CronWorkflow `news-housekeeping` (suspended; run once with `argo submit -n production --from cronworkflow/news-housekeeping`, serviceAccount argo-workflow) — carries ONLY those records through the REMAINING stages: extract → classify → enrich. Each stage selects on status ∧ rework flag (work queue,

FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, domain fairness) and settles its rows when the record leaves that stage's statuses. Settle runs at the START of a step, so budget two runs to reach zero. A reviewer's kind decides the status for every withheld kind (lnic_contracts.WITHHELD_STATUS) so the record reaches a terminal status instead of

Shared contracts: lnic_contracts (discovery_verdict · pipeline_rework · review_note · geography · coverage_floor) — pinned by tag in both repos; a behavioural release needs its consumer admission merged BEFORE the tag.
